prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International (=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase (Copperfin-approved shorter cycles; measured acceleration, no pushback surges), Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell: shares context; proposes TOBT; locks it at freeze horizon unless rule exception/authorized override recorded. Parts: Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone (stand demand, flags imbalancing TOBTs); Capacity Assessment Module (Airport Capacity Plan, Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor (Calculated Takeoff Time (CTT); priority emergency/national>scheduled>GA; no unlogged excessive delay; frozen CTT revisable on capacity update); Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove (value, confidence, reason code; frozen change needs revised code, old superseded; shall publish tower readiness changes to authenticated airline/handling users within refresh interval); Departure Metering Service (aligns TOBT/CTT; CTT→Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf: order by runway, fix, wake, spacing; in Adverse Weather/Capacity Reduction applies Business Rules Registry spacing, highlights flights likely missing CTT); North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensor; Ramp Movement Board; Contingency Operations Console; Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard (→CAM); Flight Data Exchange (intent→DMS); Airline Interface Adapter; Audit Event Ledger (old/new, user, time, authority, state; sequence history); Time Synchronization Service; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Collaborative Decision Log (manual sequence changes: user, time, flight, reason code); Common Situation Display; Identity Access Service (role-gated frozen changes, exemptions, corrections); Alert Distribution Hub; Digital Briefing Room; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner (handling capacity hard constraint); Arrival Regulation Console; deicing interface point (needs treatment/waiting pad/under treatment/released). Departure readiness indicator combines operator, handling, cockpit, route clearance, surface position. Actors: Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin (notified when resequencing erodes planned rate); Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron (Flight Intent Message, confirms TOBT, requests sequence review); Slot Coordinator=Halcyon (checks resequencing vs CTT tolerance/Slot Compliance); Airport Duty Manager; Tower Supervisor=Brindle

Document units:
S300: The feasible Target Off Block Time is therefore derived from both airside capacity and the ground service path needed to close doors, remove equipment, and start pushback without creating a conflict on the apron.
S301: Handler dispatch affects feasibility when the assigned team is still servicing another aircraft, crossing a congested apron, or waiting for security access to a remote stand.
S302: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates the Handling Resource Planner with expected service completion times so that the Regional Flow Platform can distinguish an air traffic delay from a local handling delay.
S303: The Handling Resource Planner maintains the operational view of dispatch teams, tow teams, ramp buses, belt loaders, high loaders, stairs, ground power units, air start units, and potable water equipment.
S304: The Handling Resource Planner uses the Stand Tow Request Form to reserve towing capacity and to test whether the requested movement can be completed before the proposed Target Off Block Time.
S305: If no tow team is available, the aircraft may remain blocked on stand even when the runway sequence and the Calculated Takeoff Time would otherwise support departure.
S306: Ramp buses influence feasibility for remote stands because passenger boarding cannot close until the last bus has arrived, unloaded, and cleared the stand area.
S307: Loader availability is critical for aircraft with late baggage, unit load device changes, or cargo offload requirements because the aircraft cannot be released until the hold is closed and such information remains valid.
S308: Stand equipment shortages can create hidden delay because crews may be ready and boarding may be complete while a missing tug, headset, chocks, stairs, or ground power connection prevents the off-block event.
S309: Shortages are often localized by apron sector, so the same nominal fleet of equipment can support one stand cluster while leaving another cluster unable to dispatch departures at the planned rate.
S310: For local operations displays, the Ramp Movement Board is also known as Skylark when referenced in controller training material.
S311: The Ramp Movement Board shows occupied stands, blocked service roads, and pending pushback areas so that handling constraints can be compared with the aircraft sequence before a revised time is published.
S312: The Airport CDM Portal presents the resource-driven feasibility status to the Airline Operations Coordinator and the Aircraft Operator Representative to support early negotiation rather than last-minute rejection.
S313: Brindle must confirm that any revised off-block sequence remains compatible with the Departure Metering Service before the change is released to the airport community.
